To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a large resistor between a silicon microstrip backplane and a bias supply can reduce the voltage drop between the readout strip and the silicon implant, but only for single-sided detectors.

for a single sided silicon microstrip detector with n-type bulk material, n-type silicon strip implants, and a p+ type backplane, a high value resistor between the back plane and the bias supply and a small capacitor from the backplane to ground can reduce the voltage difference between readout strips and implants to a value close to zero.

for a silicon microstrip with an AC-coupled n-type readout strip and an n-type implant strip, the voltage difference can be minimized by using an RC circuit with a large resistor and a small capacitor.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the voltage between the readout strip and the silicon strip implant is dependent on the bias supply, the backplane, and the laser power.

the voltage difference between readout strips and silicon implants on a single-sided silicon detector, with n-bulk, n-implant strips, and a backplane, can be minimized by using the following circuit components: a 1 kΩ resistor between the back plane and the bias supply; a 100 nF capacitor between the back plane to ground; a 100 Ω resistor between the readout strip and the bias supply.

the use of an AC-coupled silicon microstrip detector with a large resistor and a small capacitor connected to the backplane, and a small resistor connected to the readout strips, is the optimal configuration to minimize the voltage between the readout strip and the silicon strip implant in high radiation fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a large resistor between a detector and a bias supply, combined with a small capacitance between the backplane of the detector and ground, can be used to minimize the voltage difference between readout strips and silicon implants in a silicon microstrip device in high radiation fields.

for a single sided n-type bulk, single sided n-type implant silicon microstrip detector with an n-type backplane, a breakdown in the operational electric field is achieved at a laser power density of approximately 1 MW/cm2.

for the detector under consideration, a large resistor between backplane and bias supply, and no capacitor, is the best combination for the backplane circuitry to minimize the voltage difference between readout strips and silicon implants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the voltage on the readout strips of a microstrip detector can be controlled by adjusting the circuitry connected to the detector backplane.
the voltage difference between readout strips and silicon implants on a microstrip detector is a function of the bias voltage, laser intensity, and connected circuit components.

the voltage difference between readout strips and implant strips on a single-sided silicon detector is a function of the bias voltage, the laser power, the connected components, and the geometry of the detector.
